Trisquel GNU/Linux - Libre Fork of Ubuntu FSF Endorsed (Free Software Foundation)

Trisquel GNU/Linux is due for a major update soon. Already there is a Beta.

Only Free / Libre software is found in the Trisquel GNU/Linux repositories. (That is Free as in Freedom, not Free as in Beer.)
Even the kernel, GNU LinuxLibre, is completely free. (The Linux kernel has been non-free for many years now, with many binary blobs. The GNU LinuxLibre kernel is a completely de-blobbed fork of the Linux kernel.)

By using Trisquel GNU/Linux with, for example the fully free LibreBoot as the BIOS replacement, it is possible to run an entirely Free / Libre system.

Try it today, and provide feedback. There is a Trisquel GNU/Linux channel at Freenode, for example: #trisquel

(If you don't have Libre hardware, you might run into trouble with wi-fi connectivity, or ethernet card, so download any .deb files you may require, and their dependencies, in advance and keep them handy on a USB drive or somewhere.)

I used Trisquel for a bit. Really give you an eye opening experience on how much your machine depends on the closed binary blobs. Tossed it on my Lenovo T410 and had a few things just not function (WiFi, Bluetooth, etc.). Crazy how we depend on these blobs.
